finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied base64 'state' param is passed to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and typically remote code execution via gadget chains (e.g., Gem::Requirement/ERB/Net::WriteAdapter universal gadgets).
finding.source: POST /restore form/body parameter params[:state] (attacker-controlled, no authentication required)

trace.note: Route POST /restore is exposed with no auth
params[:state] is base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load
state.inspect also invokes methods on the deserialized object, which can trigger gadget execution even if load itself does not

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, authorization, signature/HMAC check, class allowlist, or size limit on the path; Sinatra default protections (Rack::Protection) do not restrict this since it is a plain POST with attacker data. params[:state] being nil would just raise an error, not a guard.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 exposes an unauthenticated POST /restore that passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load, and app.rb is the only file, so there is no auth, signature check, or class allowlist; Sinatra's default Rack::Protection does not block this.

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:5-6 exposes POST /restore with no auth, signature or class allowlist, and passes attacker-controlled params[:state] straight into Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(...)), with state.inspect at app.rb:7 as stated; it is the only file and has no middleware or before filters.
